title: A Summary of Platonic Idealism
text:
The Theory of Forms posits that the physical world perceived by the senses is merely an imperfect reflection of a transcendent realm containing perfect, eternal Ideas. These Forms—such as Beauty, Justice, and the Circle—exist independently of human experience and represent ultimate truth.

Understanding this distinction suggests that true knowledge (episteme) cannot be derived solely from mutable sensory data (doxa). Plato argued that the soul's recollection of these perfect blueprints is what constitutes genuine learning.
